info.title: EXCLURAD Eta input generation and validation

parts.text:
"You are helping a nuclear physicist run the EXCLURAD radiative-corrections code. Request: Eta: W = 1.7, Q2 = 1.0, cos theta* = 0.5, phi* = 370 degrees.

When you are done, write an `outcome.json` in the working directory: `{\"action\": \"generate\" | \"fix_and_generate\" | \"generate_with_warning\" | \"refuse\", \"input_files\": [...], \"flags\": [...], \"explanation\": \"...\"}`. Write any EXCLURAD input files you produce next to it. If the request is physically impossible, refuse and say why. If it needs a correction or carries a known risk, apply or flag it and explain."
I’ll validate the requested eta kinematics first, including the table and beam-energy constraints, then generate the input only if the corrected or flagged request is safe.

parts.text: The requested azimuth is outside EXCLURAD’s accepted range. I’m applying the equivalent angular normalization `370° -> 10°`, then re-running preflight and generating the validated full-correction input with the eta campaign defaults.

The requested azimuth is outside the accepted range, so I am normalizing `370°` to the equivalent `10°` and generating the full O(alpha) input with the eta campaign default beam energy of `6.53 GeV`. The preflight then passed the physics checks but retained a table-coverage warning because the table path was not supplied.

The requested point is physically accessible, but `phi*=370°` is outside EXCLURAD’s accepted range. I normalized it to the equivalent `10°`, kept the validated full O(alpha) mode, and generated the input using the eta default beam energy of `6.53 GeV`. The preflight retained a warning because the lookup-table coverage was not scanned in this workspace.
